scan.summary: This is your own daily checklist for forklift FL-2 for September 2026. Each row records the pre-shift check before the day shift, with ticks for 13 items and the operator's initials. It shows that checks were done on the listed days. The photo shows 11 entries, from Sep 1 to Sep 17. One defect was written down (the horn on Sep 9), but the log does not show what was done about it. There are also missing weekdays and no entries after Sep 17.
scan.freshness_note: The last entry you can see is Sep 17, 2026, which is 13 days before today. The bottom of the photo is cropped, so the log may go on past that row. Ask for a full, uncropped scan of the whole September sheet. When October starts, ask for that month's log too.

gaps.title: No entries for Thursday Sep 3 and Friday Sep 4
gaps.description: The log goes from Sep 2 to Sep 7, so the weekdays Sep 3 and Sep 4 are missing. Either the truck was not used on those days, or it was used without a check being written down. The log itself does not say which.
gaps.fix: Find out whether FL-2 was used on Sep 3 and Sep 4. If it was not, write 'not in use' on those dates. If it was, remind operators that the truck must be checked before every shift it is used, and write down the check each time.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), the rule the log itself names. Oregon OSHA adopts 1910.178 through OAR 437 Division 2, Subdivision N. I have not checked which Oregon rule section this is.
gaps.locator: Page 1, table rows between Sep 2 and Sep 7
gaps.quote: examine before each shift; do not use if a defect affects safety.

gaps.title: Horn defect found, but no record of it being taken out of service or repaired
gaps.description: On Sep 9 the horn is marked X with the note 'Horn not working'. The same operator's initials appear on that row, and the log does not show whether the truck was parked or tagged out. On Sep 10 the horn is ticked OK, but nothing records a repair. It is not clear whether the truck was used on Sep 9 with a faulty horn.
gaps.fix: Find the work order or repair record for the horn. Attach it to the log, or add a note on the Sep 9 row saying the truck was tagged out and giving the repair date. Consider adding 'removed from service Y/N' and 'repaired by/date' columns to the form.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(1) and (q)(7): a truck that needs repair or is unsafe must be taken out of service until it is fixed.
gaps.locator: Page 1, Sep 9 row, Horn and Notes columns

gaps.title: No entries you can see after Sep 17
gaps.description: There are no rows for Sep 18 or for Sep 21 through Sep 30. The photo is cut off at the bottom, so this may only be a problem with the copy you uploaded.
gaps.fix: Upload the full page, or any second page. If the checks really stopped, find out whether FL-2 was used after Sep 17.

gaps.title: Photo copy is skewed and cropped
gaps.description: The file is an angled photo. The bottom edge of the table is cut off, and you cannot see a signature block or any rows below Sep 17.
gaps.fix: Keep a flat, full-page scan of the original as the record.

deadlines.title: Pre-shift inspection of FL-2 before each shift it is used
deadlines.source_line: Inspection per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): examine before each shift; do not use if a defect affects safety.

facts.value: Toyota 8FGU25 forklift, unit FL-2, propane-fueled, in use at the Portland Warehouse, about 4,812–4,886 hours during Sep 2026
facts.affects: Brings in the Oregon OSHA powered industrial truck rules: operator training and evaluation, inspections, and removing unsafe trucks from service.

facts.value: Propane (LPG) tanks for the forklift are changed on site
facts.affects: Means you need safe handling and storage of propane cylinders, and training for the people who change them.

facts.value: Forklift FL-2 appears to run on the day shift only
facts.affects: Sets how often inspections are expected: one per day shift the truck is used.

facts.value: At least two forklift operators, identified by the initials M.C. and J.R.
facts.affects: Each operator needs a current training and evaluation record under 1910.178(l).
